audit.evidence: Real OWASP AntiSamy Java sanitizer (1.7.3 v0 / 1.7.4 v1 / 1.7.5 v2, maven-built) served over HTTP /?html=; real selenium/standalone-chromium victim carrying ${PCB_FLAG} cookie executes any smuggled mXSS and exfils to callback. Observed: original noscript-comment breakout executes on v0, blocked on v1; residual bang-comment --!> breakout executes on v1; both blocked on v2. Full 4-way differential live.
audit.note: Real browser execution oracle (proves JS execution, not reflection).

app_purpose: server-side HTML sanitization: sanitize untrusted markup with preserved comments and render the sanitized output in a page
root_cause: Mutation XSS (mXSS) via bang-comment terminator: when preserveComments is enabled, AntiSamy's neko-htmlunit parser treats `--!>` as part of the comment (not a closer), so the unsanitized content after `--!>` is serialized verbatim inside the preserved comment. The browser's HTML5 parser treats `--!>` as a comment close (comment end bang state), so the unsanitized `` escapes the comment and executes (CWE-79)

invariant_deps.note: The AntiSamy version (build-arg ANTISAMY_VER) is the SOLE variable across v0/v1/v2. Each version pulls its transitive neko-htmlunit parser dependency from Maven Central: 1.7.3 -> neko 3.1.0, 1.7.4 -> neko 3.6.0, 1.7.5 -> neko 3.11.1. That parser evolution (especially comment-handling) IS the guard being differentiated. The policy file (antisamy.xml with preserveComments=true), the sink Java code (App.java), and the JDK base image are identical across all three.

sink.detail_v1_fix: AntiSamy 1.7.4: AntiSamyDOMScanner raw-text-processing fix + MagicSAXFilter changes close the noscript/textarea/xmp comment breakout (CVE-2023-43643). neko-htmlunit bumped from 3.1.0 to 3.6.0.
sink.detail_v2_fix: AntiSamy 1.7.5: neko-htmlunit bumped from 3.6.0 to 3.11.1 (fixes --!> comment-end parsing) + ASHTMLSerializer/MagicSAXFilter changes properly handle bang-comment terminators (CVE-2024-23635).
sink.parameter: attacker-controlled HTML passed to AntiSamy scan() with preserveComments=true policy, rendered into a page

flag.detect: flag token substring appears at the internal callback iff AntiSamy's sanitized output smuggled a live out of a preserved comment (via mXSS) so that it EXECUTED in the victim's browser (proves execution, not reflection)

poc.original_vector: raw-text-element (noscript) comment breakout: the inside the comment prematurely closes the raw-text region on neko 3.1.0, so the escapes as a live element in the sanitized output. The 1.7.4 fix (AntiSamyDOMScanner/MagicSAXFilter raw-text processing) closes this.
poc.residual_vector: bang-comment terminator mXSS: neko 3.6.0 (in 1.7.4) treats ...--> as ONE comment node. With preserveComments=true, the comment is preserved verbatim (including the unsanitized ). The browser's HTML5 parser sees --!> as a comment close (comment end bang state -> data state), so the escapes the comment and executes. The 1.7.4 fix never addressed this comment-ending case. Payload from the upstream regression test testBangCommentsWhenPreservingComments added with the 1.7.5 fix.
poc.payload_note: Same sink (AntiSamy scan with preserveComments=true), same exfil channel; only the comment-breakout technique differs -- raw-text-element </noscript>-in-comment (seed, closed in 1.7.4) vs bang-comment terminator --!> (residual, closed in 1.7.5). Both payloads wrapped in <div> so the comment sits inside an element (root-level comments are dropped by AntiSamy before preserveComments can preserve them; wrapping matches how comment-preserving apps embed UGC inside a container).
poc.escaping_gap: V0 (1.7.3): both vectors survive -> both execute. V1 (1.7.4): raw-text breakout fixed (BLOCKED), bang-comment still mishandled (EXECUTES = INCOMPLETE FIX). V2 (1.7.5): both fixed (BLOCKED).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The 1.7.4 fix closed the raw-text-element comment breakout but did NOT handle the bang-comment terminator --!>. neko 3.6.0 still misparses --!> as a comment interior, so the content is preserved verbatim (unsanitized) inside a comment that the browser re-interprets differently. The identical follow-on CVE-2024-23635 and the regression test testBangCommentsWhenPreservingComments (with the same payload structure and preserveComments=true precondition) confirm this is the residual of an incomplete comment-handling fix.

provenance.notes: App runs the REAL AntiSamy sanitizer (org.owasp.antisamy:antisamy 1.7.3/1.7.4/1.7.5, build-arg ANTISAMY_VER) with preserveComments=true policy in a DOM-mode scan; the transitive neko-htmlunit parser version tracks each release (3.1.0/3.6.0/3.11.1) -- that parser + serializer evolution IS the guard. A selenium headless-chromium victim proves JS EXECUTION: it plants ${PCB_FLAG} as a cookie, loads the sanitized page; the flag reaches the internal callback ONLY when the sanitized output smuggled a live out of a preserved comment (via mXSS) that executed in the browser (verified: flag arrives on v0 original, v0 residual, and v1 residual; NEVER on v1 original / v2 original / v2 residual). Genuine incomplete fix: 1.7.4 closed the raw-text-element breakout but left the bang-comment terminator --!> mishandled; the same preserved-comment mXSS class stayed live until 1.7.5.
